table_context_mentions_column_and_precis.original_text: business_logic: '- Load all rows from staging.stg_google_ads__keyword_stats (ks). - Join dimensional data: - Join to staging.stg_google_ads__ad_group_history (agi) filtered to is_most_recent_record = true on ad_group_id and source_relation. - Join to staging.stg_google_ads__campaign_history (ci) filtered to is_most_recent_record = true on campaign_id and source_relation. - Compute per-row performance metrics (rounding to 4 decimals unless noted; NULL policies explicit): - ctr: if impressions > 0 → (clicks / impressions) * 100; else 0; rounded 4 decimals; unit = percentage (0+). - cpc: if clicks > 0 → spend / clicks; else 0; rounded 4 decimals. - cpm: if impressions > 0 → spend / impressions * 1000; else 0; rounded 4 decimals. - cost_per_conversion: if conversions > 0 → spend / conversions; else NULL; rounded 4 decimals. - roas: if spend > 0 and conversions_value > 0 → conversions_value / spend; else 0; rounded 4 decimals. - conversion_rate: if clicks > 0 → (conversions / clicks) * 100; else 0; rounded 4 decimals; unit = percentage (0+). - Compute lifetime cumulative metrics using window sums partitioned by (keyword_id = ks.criterion_id, ad_group_id) ordered by date_day, rows unbounded preceding: - lifetime_spend, lifetime_clicks, lifetime_conversions, lifetime_conversions_value. - Compute days_since_first_activity: number of days between the first date in the (keyword_id, ad_group_id) partition and the current date_day; non-negative integer. - Compute campaign-level benchmarks over (partition by campaign_id, date_day): - campaign_avg_ctr, campaign_avg_cpc, campaign_avg_conversion_rate, campaign_avg_roas (simple averages of per-row metrics). - Percentile ranks: ctr_percentile_in_campaign = percent_rank ordered by ctr ascending; conv_rate_percentile_in_campaign = percent_rank ordered by conversion_rate ascending; roas_percentile_in_campaign = percent_rank ordered by roas descending; range [0,1]. - Derive segmentation and recommendations: - ctr_vs_campaign_pct: if campaign_avg_ctr > 0 → ((ctr - campaign_avg_ctr) / campaign_avg_ctr) * 100; else NULL; rounded 2 decimals. - roas_vs_campaign_pct: if campaign_avg_roas > 0 → ((roas - campaign_avg_roas) / campaign_avg_roas) * 100; else NULL; rounded 2 decimals. - keyword_maturity_stage by days_since_first_activity: <7 → "New Keyword"; <30 → "Testing Phase"; <90 → "Optimization Phase"; <365 → "Mature Keyword"; else "Legacy Keyword". - performance_tier based on percentiles (evaluated in listed order; first match wins): ctr_pct >= 0.8 and conv_pct >= 0.8 → "Star Performer"; ctr_pct >= 0.6 and conv_pct >= 0.6 → "Strong Performer"; ctr_pct >= 0.4 and conv_pct >= 0.4 → "Average Performer"; ctr_pct >= 0.2 or conv_pct >= 0.2 → "Weak Performer"; else "Poor Performer". - bid_recommendation: roas > campaign_avg_roas*1.5 and ctr > campaign_avg_ctr*1.2 → "Increase Bid (+20%)"; roas > campaign_avg_roas*1.2 and ctr > campaign_avg_ctr → "Increase Bid (+10%)"; roas < campaign_avg_roas*0.7 and ctr < campaign_avg_ctr*0.8 → "Decrease Bid (-20%)"; roas < campaign_avg_roas*0.8 and ctr < campaign_avg_ctr → "Decrease Bid (-10%)"; conversions = 0 and days_since_first_activity > 30 → "Consider Pausing"; else "Maintain Bid". - efficiency_score: treat any missing percentile as 0, weight (ctr 30, conv_rate 40, roas 30), clamp to [0,100]; final output rounded to 1 decimal. - volume_tier by lifetime_spend: <100 → "Low Volume"; <1000 → "Medium Volume"; <5000 → "High Volume"; else "Premium Volume". - value_tier by lifetime_conversions_value: <500 → "Low Value"; <2500 → "Medium Value"; <10000 → "High Value"; else "Premium Value". - Derive quality/ops flags (always non-NULL booleans): - data_quality_flag: clicks > impressions. - optimization_needed_flag: spend > 100 and conversions = 0 and days_since_first_activity > 14. - scale_opportunity_flag: roas > 5 and ctr > campaign_avg_ctr * 1.5. - pause_candidate_flag: efficiency_score < 20 and days_since_first_activity > 30. - Final filter (rows must satisfy): spend >= 0, clicks >= 0, impressions >= 0, conversions >= 0, and date_day, keyword_id, ad_group_id, campaign_id are NOT NULL. - Output rows are ordered by keyword_id, ad_group_id, date_day; no de-duplication beyond the final filter.'

table_context_mentions_column_and_precis.original_text: business_logic: '- Build base from intermediate.int_hubspot__deals_enhanced: - Select deal, pipeline, owner, and timestamp fields; rename amount to deal_amount and closed_date to close_date. - deal_cycle_time_days: number of whole days from created_date to close_date when both exist; otherwise NULL. - deal_status: - Won: closed_date present and amount > 0 - Lost: closed_date present and amount = 0 - Open: closed_date absent - Unknown: any other case (e.g., closed with negative or NULL amount) - deal_size_category: - Enterprise (100K+): amount >= 100000 - Large (50K-100K): 50000–<100000 - Medium (10K-50K): 10000–<50000 - Small (<10K): >0–<10000 - No Value: amount <= 0 or NULL - created_year/created_quarter are extracted from created_date; closed_year/closed_quarter are extracted only when close_date exists. - Compute pipeline_stage_analysis grouped by (deal_pipeline, deal_pipeline_stage), excluding NULL stage IDs: - deals_in_stage: number of deals in the group. - won_from_stage / lost_from_stage: counts where status is Won / Lost. - stage_win_rate: percentage of group deals that are Won (0–100); 0 when the denominator would be zero. - total_stage_value: sum of deal_amount; averages computed over non-NULL amounts. - avg_stage_cycle_time: average cycle time for Won deals only. - median_stage_cycle_time: continuous median (50th percentile) of non-NULL cycle times in the group. - Compute quarterly_performance_trends grouped by (created_year, created_quarter), including only rows with both present: - quarterly_deals_created: number of deals created in the cohort. - quarterly_deal_value_created: sum of deal_amount (NULL if all amounts are NULL). - same_quarter_wins: count of deals that were created and closed Won in the same year-quarter. - same_quarter_revenue: sum of deal_amount for those same-quarter Wins (0 when none in the cohort). - same_quarter_conversion_rate: percentage of cohort deals that closed Won in the same quarter (0–100); 0 when the cohort size is zero. - Left join stage metrics on (deal_pipeline, deal_pipeline_stage) and quarterly metrics on (created_year, created_quarter). - If a join has no match (e.g., stage ID or created_date is NULL), all joined metrics from that source are NULL. - Output one row per deal_id with base fields plus matched stage and quarterly metrics; percentages are 0–100 with no rounding; standard aggregates ignore NULL inputs.'

table_context_mentions_column_and_precis.original_text: business_logic: '- Load survey_performance with survey_id, survey_name, survey_status, total_responses, completed_responses, completion_rate, and avg_completion_time_seconds. - Load response_quality with survey_id, response_id, include_in_analysis, quality_score, and overall_quality_rating. - Build a quality_summary per survey_id: - total_assessed_responses = number of distinct response_id values. - high_quality_responses = number of responses where include_in_analysis is true; false or null are not counted. - avg_quality_score = average of quality_score values; records with null quality_score are ignored; no rounding. - excellent_responses = number of responses where overall_quality_rating equals "High Quality" (exact string match). - Left join survey_performance to quality_summary by survey_id. - When quality_summary is missing, set avg_quality_score, high_quality_responses, and excellent_responses to 0; if avg_quality_score is null, use 0. - Compute quality_adjusted_completion_rate: - If total_responses > 0 and total_assessed_responses > 0, multiply completion_rate by the fraction high_quality_responses / total_responses (fractional division; no truncation); otherwise use completion_rate; if completion_rate is null, the result is null. - Assign performance_tier using inclusive thresholds: - High Performer when completion_rate ≥ 0.8 and avg_quality_score (using 0 when missing) ≥ 80. - Good Performer when completion_rate ≥ 0.6 and avg_quality_score (using 0 when missing) ≥ 60. - Average Performer when completion_rate ≥ 0.4. - Otherwise Needs Improvement. - Compute roi_score as completion_rate * 60 plus avg_quality_score (using 0 when missing) * 0.4; if completion_rate is null, roi_score is null; no rounding. - Set analysis_date to the current timestamp (same value for all rows in a run). - Filter out surveys where total_responses ≤ 0 or total_responses is null. - Order the final output by roi_score descending.'

table_context_mentions_column_and_precis.original_text: business_logic: '- Build job_applications: - Join job to job_application to application; include only applications where applied_at is populated. - Group by job_id, job_title, job_status, job_created_at, and applied_at year and quarter (quarter 1–4). - Compute: - total_applications: count of application rows. - unique_candidates: count of distinct candidate_id. - hired_count: count of applications with status "hired". - active_count: count of applications with status "active". - rejected_count: count of applications with a rejection timestamp present. - avg_process_days: average days from applied_at to rejected_at if present, otherwise to last_activity_at; exclude non-computable durations; no rounding. - Build interview_metrics: - From job_application joined to application (applied_at populated), left join scheduled_interview and scorecard. - Group by job_id and applied_at year and quarter. - Compute: - total_interviews: distinct count of scheduled_interview_id. - completed_interviews: count of scheduled interviews with status "completed" (not distinct). - total_scorecards: distinct count of scorecard_id. - avg_interview_score: average of mapped recommendations across scorecards (strong_yes=4, yes=3, no=2, definitely_not=1); exclude other values and nulls; no rounding. - Join metrics: - Left join interview_metrics to job_applications on job_id, application_year, and application_quarter. - If interview_metrics is missing, set total_interviews, completed_interviews, and total_scorecards to 0; keep avg_interview_score as NULL. - Derive rates (percentages 0–100, double precision, no rounding): - hire_rate: hired_count divided by total_applications times 100; return 0 if the denominator is 0. - interview_rate: total_interviews divided by total_applications times 100; return 0 if the denominator is 0. - interview_to_hire_rate: hired_count divided by total_interviews times 100; return 0 if the denominator is 0. - interview_completion_rate: completed_interviews divided by total_interviews times 100; return 0 if the denominator is 0. - Assign performance_tier (first matching rule applies): - "Excellent" if hired_count >= 3 and hire_rate >= 20. - "Good" if hired_count >= 2 and hire_rate >= 15. - "Average" if hired_count >= 1 and hire_rate >= 10. - "Needs Improvement" if total_applications >= 10. - Else "Low Activity". - Flags: - is_fast_process: 1 if avg_process_days <= 30 else 0; NULL avg_process_days yields 0. - has_good_interview_quality: 1 if avg_interview_score >= 3.0 else 0; NULL avg_interview_score yields 0. - Final filter and ordering: - Keep only rows where total_applications >= 1. - Order rows by application_year descending, application_quarter descending, then hire_rate descending.'

table_context_mentions_column_and_precis.original_text: business_logic: '- Keep applications where applied_at and source_id are present. - Enrich with source_name and source_type via a left join on source_id; if no source match, name/type are NULL. - Derive application_year and application_quarter from applied_at. - Group by source_id, source_name, source_type, application_year, application_quarter. - Aggregations per group: * total_applications: number of application rows. * unique_candidates: count of distinct non-null candidate_id values. * total_hires: applications with status exactly "hired" (string match is exact and case-sensitive). * active_applications: applications with status exactly "active". * rejected_applications: applications where rejected_at is present. * applications_with_interviews: applications that have at least one scheduled interview linked by application_id; each application counted once regardless of interview count. * avg_process_days: for each application, compute days from applied_at to rejected_at if present, otherwise to last_activity_at; average these durations; applications lacking both end timestamps do not contribute. - Metrics (expressed as percentages from 0 to 100, no rounding): * hire_rate: total_hires divided by total_applications; 0 if total_applications is 0. * interview_rate: applications_with_interviews divided by total_applications; 0 if total_applications is 0. * interview_to_hire_rate: total_hires divided by applications_with_interviews; 0 if no interviewed applications. * rejection_rate: rejected_applications divided by total_applications; 0 if total_applications is 0. - Rankings per year-quarter: * hire_rate_rank: rank by hire_rate descending (ties share rank; gaps allowed). * volume_rank: rank by total_applications descending (ties share rank; gaps allowed). - performance_tier: assign in order—High Performer (hire_rate ≥ 20 and total_applications ≥ 10), Good Performer (hire_rate ≥ 10 and total_applications ≥ 5), High Volume (total_applications ≥ 10), Medium Volume (total_applications ≥ 5), else Low Volume. - efficiency_score: if total_applications > 0, hire_rate + (total_applications ÷ 10); otherwise 0; no rounding. - Exclude groups with total_applications < 1. - Order rows by application_year descending, application_quarter descending, then efficiency_score descending.'

table_context_mentions_column_and_precis.original_text: business_logic: '- Start from intermediate.int_xero__general_ledger_fact, keeping rows where journal_date is present; select journal_date (cast to DATE), account_code, account_name, account_type, account_class, net_amount, region, department, project. - Create a continuous daily date spine from the minimum to the maximum journal_date (inclusive) at 1-day intervals. - For each date in the spine and for each combination of account_code, account_name, account_type, account_class, region, department, and project found in the ledger up to that date, compute a running_balance as the cumulative sum of net_amount for all ledger rows with journal_date on or before the report_date. Combinations with no prior activity yield no output after filtering (no backfilling before first activity). - Derive categories from account attributes: - balance_sheet_category: ASSET→"Assets"; LIABILITY→"Liabilities"; EQUITY/REVENUE/EXPENSE→"Equity"; anything else→"Other" (NULLs map to "Other"). - balance_sheet_subcategory: ASSET with type BANK or CURRENT→"Current Assets"; ASSET with type FIXED→"Fixed Assets"; LIABILITY with type CURRLIAB or TERMLIAB→"Liabilities"; EQUITY→"Equity"; anything else→"Other" (NULLs map to "Other"). - Keep only rows where running_balance is not equal to zero; rows with zero or NULL running_balance are excluded. - Set amount = running_balance. - Compute totals after filtering: - category_total = the sum of amount across all rows with the same report_date and balance_sheet_category. - subcategory_total = the sum of amount across all rows with the same report_date and balance_sheet_subcategory. - Set report_generated_at to the current timestamp at query time. The final ORDER BY (report_date DESC, then category, subcategory, account_code) is for presentation only.'

table_context_mentions_column_and_precis.original_text: business_logic: '- Start from staging.stg_youtube__channel_demographics using date_day, video_id, country_code, age_group, views_percentage. - Keep only age_group in {''13-17'',''18-24'',''25-34'',''35-44'',''45-54'',''55-64'',''65-''}. - Aggregate views_percentage by (date_day, video_id, country_code, age_group) to get views_pct: - Null inputs are ignored in the sum; if all inputs are null for a group, views_pct is null. - Multiple rows for the same keys are combined by summation only. - For each (date_day, video_id, country_code), compute pct_sum as the sum of views_pct across the kept age groups: - Null views_pct are ignored; pct_sum is null only when all views_pct are null in the partition. - Normalize per age_group: - If pct_sum > 0, set pct_norm = views_pct / pct_sum and clamp to the range [0.0, 1.0]. - If pct_sum <= 0 or pct_sum is null, set pct_norm = 0.0. - No rounding; double precision is retained. - Pivot to age columns (''13-17'',''18-24'',''25-34'',''35-44'',''45-54'',''55-64'',''65-'') by summing pct_norm for rows matching each age label within (date_day, video_id, country_code): - If no row exists for an age label, the column is null. - If a row exists but pct_sum <= 0 or pct_sum is null, the column is 0.0. - If pct_sum > 0 but that age group’s views_pct is missing, the column is null (because pct_norm is null). - Set pct_total_before_normalization to the total of views_pct across the kept age groups for the (date_day, video_id, country_code); it is null only when all views_pct are null. - Output includes only (date_day, video_id, country_code) combinations that have at least one kept age group after filtering.'
